```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
```

## Airnbnb

```{r}
data("nyc_airbnb")

nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(
    stars = review_scores_location / 2
  ) |> 
  rename(
    borough = neighbourhood_group,
    neighborhood = neighbourhood
  ) |> 
  filter(
    borough != "Staten Island"
  ) |> 
  select(price, stars, borough, neighborhood, room_type)
```

Fit a Linear Regression

```{r}
fit = lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = nyc_airbnb)
```

Look at the Results

```{r}
fit
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
fitted.values(fit) # will print out all 40,000 fitted values
resid(fit)

names(fit)
names(summary(fit)) # allows you to analyze different statistics from summary
```

Most of this Output is Bad; Let's Use Broom

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit) |>
  select(-std.error) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

broom::glance(fit)
```

Change the Reference Category

```{r}
fit =
  nyc_airbnb |>
  mutate(
    borough = fct_infreq(borough)
  ) |>
  lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = _)

broom::tidy(fit) |>
  select(-std.error, -statistic) |>
  mutate(term = str_replace(term, "borough", "Borough: ")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Diagnostics

Diagnostics refers to anaylzing the Residuals

```{r}
modelr::add_residuals(nyc_airbnb, fit)
```


```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>                               # creates a scatterplot of skewed residual distribution, not constant
  modelr::add_residuals(fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = stars, y = resid)) +
  geom_point()

nyc_airbnb |>                               # creates a violin plot of skewed residual distribution, not constant                      
  modelr::add_residuals(fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = borough, y = resid)) +
  geom_violin()
```

## Hypothesis Testing

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit) |>
  mutate(term = str_replace(term, "borough", "Borough: ")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Try Testing Nested Models

```{r}
fit_null = lm(price ~ stars, data = nyc_airbnb)
fit_alt = lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = nyc_airbnb)

anova(fit_null, fit_alt)
```

## Nesting Data

Trying More Complicated Models

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  lm(price ~ stars * borough + room_type * borough, data = _) |> # tests the interaction between stars and boroughs, asks whether number of stars affects room type between boroughs
  broom::tidy() |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Determining What's Happening in Manhattan

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |>
  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = _) |>
  broom::tidy()
  
  nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Bronx") |>
  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = _) |>
  broom::tidy()
```

Let's Fix This With Iteration

```{r}
airbnb_lm = function(data) {

  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = data)
  
}
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  nest(datasets = -borough) |>
  mutate(
    fits = map(datasets, airbnb_lm),
    results = map(fits, broom::tidy)      # tidies up the results of each linear model fits
  ) |>
  select(-datasets, -fits) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  select(borough, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term,
    values_from = estimate
  )
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  nest(datasets = -borough) |>
  mutate(
    fits = map(datasets, \(data) lm(price ~ stars, data = data)), # acts as a shorthand for this function
    results = map(fits, broom::tidy)
  ) |>
  select(-datasets, -fits) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  select(borough, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term,
    values_from = estimate
  )
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |>
  nest(datasets = -neighborhood) |>
  mutate(
    fits = map(datasets, \(df) lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = df)),
    results = map(fits, broom::tidy)
  ) |>
  select(neighborhood, results) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  filter(term == "room_typePrivate room") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = neighborhood, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 80, hjust = 1))
```

## Logistic Regression

Importing the WP Homicide Data

```{r}
baltimore_df = 
  read_csv("data/homicide-data.csv") |>
  filter(city == "Baltimore") |>
  mutate(
    resolved = as.numeric(disposition == "Closed by arrest"),
    victim_age = as.numeric(victim_age)
  )
```

Fit the Logistic Regression

```{r}
fit_logistic = 
  baltimore_df |>
  mutate(victim_race = fct_infreq(victim_race)) |>
  glm(resolved ~ victim_age + victim_race, data = _, family = binomial())

fit_logistic |>
  broom::tidy() |>
  mutate(OR = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(term, OR, estimate, p.value) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
